title: Randomness from initial conditions: The challenge of incompleteness
summary: Certain prima facie deterministic theories, notably Bohmian mechanics and kinetic theory, require ``random'' initial conditions in order to achieve their goals. I analyze recent proposals that this idea should be implemented using algorithmic randomness, seen as a mathematical sharpening of the typicality arguments originally used to understand these theories. On the one hand my analysis includes a critique of these arguments and hence a defense of this sharpening.
